top_comments: It seems `14.2.2` fixed this for development but not for prod.
@GabenGar Thanks for sharing a —we will be taking a look at this!

We are seeing the same issue on `14.2.2` where on production builds the CSS styles get included in an unexpected order. 

The specific example we are seeing is that CSS styles imported into layout.js are overriding CSS styles set in a component level stylesheet even though they have the same CSS specificity and the component CSS should override the layout's CSS. This bug appears to be due to the order that the CSS is included in the final static .css files that are included in the production build.

title: i18n configuration causes 500 error when certain malformed URLs are visited
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Parker-Echo/nextjs-reproduction-app-bug

### To Reproduce

1. Start the server `next dev`.
2. Run `curl -k http://localhost:3000/\\\\\\%20../%20../%20../%20../%20../%20../foobar`
3. Observe it returns a 500 error and logs the following
```
Failed to handle request for /\\\%20../%20../%20../%20../%20../%20../foobar
TypeError: Invalid URL
    at new URL (node:internal/url:775:36)
    at parseRelativeUrl (my-app/node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/router/utils/parse-relative-url.js:16:68)
    at parseUrl (my-app/node_modules/next/dist/shared/lib/router/utils/parse-url.js:15:55)
    at requestHandlerImpl (my-app/node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/router-server.js:115:54)
    at Server.requestListener (my-app/node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/start-server.js:141:19)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5) {
  code: 'ERR_INVALID_URL',
  input: '/\\\\\\%20../%20../%20../%20../%20../%20../etc/passwd/',
  base: 'http://n/'
}
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Following the steps from the previous section, I expect a redirect or a 404 error.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 23.6.0: Mon Jul 29 21:14:30 PDT 2024; root:xnu-10063.141.2~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
  Available memory (MB): 16384
  Available CPU cores: 10
Binaries:
  Node: 20.9.0
  npm: 10.1.0
  Yarn: 1.22.19
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 15.0.0-canary.183 // Latest available version is detected (15.0.0-canary.183).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.0.0-rc-2d16326d-20240930
  react-dom: 19.0.0-rc-2d16326d-20240930
  typescript: 5.3.3
Next.js Config:
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not sure, Internationalization (i18n), Runtime

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next start (local), Other (Deployed)

### Additional context

I don't repro if I access the URL via postman or the browser, possibly because of different encodings. I reproduced against 14.2 as well. Only happens with i18n configured. 
Forum post: https://nextjs-forum.com/post/1293815757494288404
top_comments:
Hi! I'm working on a fix for this issue, picking up where @aurmartin's #71281 left off (closed without the test case requested by @ijjk).

Reproduced on Next.js 16.2.4 (latest stable) and 16.3.0-canary.4. While the HTTP response is a 308 redirect, the server logs are flooded with `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_URL]: Invalid URL` on every malformed request — noisy in production and a potential DoS surface.

Plan:
- Same fix as #71281: use `normalizeRepeatedSlashes` instead of `replace(/^\/+/, '/')` in `router-server.ts`
- Add an e2e test covering the original repro and a few related malformed URL patterns

Will open a draft PR shortly. Credit to @aurmartin for the original investigation and fix.

title: useContext is null during SSG prerender in pnpm workspace (App Router, Next 14.2.x & 16 canary)
body:
# Title `useContext` is null during SSG prerender in pnpm workspace (App Router, Next 14.2.x) # Body ### Verify canary release - [x] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release Tested on `next@canary` resolving to **16.2.1-canary.43** with **React 19.0.0** — reproduces identically with the same `useContext` null error (`.next/server/chunks/ssr/[root-of-the-server]__*.js`). The bug is not a Next 14 regression; it spans at least Next 14.2.0, 14.2.35, and 16.2.1-canary.43. ### Provide environment information ``` Operating System: Platform: win32 Arch: x64 Version: Windows 11 Home Single Language 10.0.26200 Binaries: Node: 20.x pnpm: 10.15.0 Relevant Packages: next: tested on 14.2.0, 14.2.35, and canary (16.2.1-canary.43) — all reproduce react: tested on 18.2.0 and 19.0.0 — both reproduce react-dom: matched to react version TypeScript: 5.4.x Package manager: pnpm (workspace mode, 2-app minimal repro) ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? App Router, Output (export/standalone), Runtime ### Which stage(s) are affected? `next build` (local), `next build` (Vercel) ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/saasmeld-holdco/next-ssg-usecontext-repro ```bash git clone https://github.com/saasmeld-holdco/next-ssg-usecontext-repro cd next-ssg-usecontext-repro pnpm install pnpm --filter app-a build # Crashes during "Generating static pages" with useContext null. ``` Verified reproducing on `next@14.2.35` with `react@18.2.0` pinned via pnpm overrides (single React instance confirmed via `readlink`). ### To Reproduce 1. Create a pnpm workspace with 4 Next 14.2.x apps sharing a `@saasmeld/ui` package via `workspace:*`. 2. Each app's root layout wraps `children` in `NextIntlClientProvider` plus a small `PostHogProvider` that uses `usePathname()`. 3. Run `pnpm --filter @saasmeld/web build`. Note: a fully stripped layout (no providers, no hooks, no intl) and a trivial `

` homepage **still reproduce the crash**. The issue is not provider-specific. ### Expected Behavior `next build` completes SSG for all static routes and emits `.next/` artifacts. ### Actual Behavior On Next 14.2.x: ``` Generating static pages (0/39) ... TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext') at t.useContext (.../next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-page.runtime.prod.js:12:109363) at d (.../apps/web/.next/server/chunks/846.js:66:22885) at p (.../apps/web/.next/server/chunks/846.js:66:14872) at au (.../next/dist/compiled/next-server/app-page.runtime.dev.js:35:10446) ... Error occurred prerendering page "/". Read more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/prerender-error ``` On Next 16.2.1-canary.43 + React 19 (same error, different compiled chunk path): ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext') at (.../app-a/.next/server/chunks/ssr/[root-of-the-server]__*.js:4:28956) { digest: '2041833152' } Export encountered an error on /_global-error/page: /_global-error, exiting the build. ``` Every static route fails with the identical error. On Next 14, the compiled chunk offset 27451 decodes to Next's own `usePathname()` context lookup inside an error-boundary wrapper — the React dispatcher is `null` at that point. ### Things attempted that did NOT fix it - Pinning React + react-dom to 18.2.0 via pnpm `overrides` (confirmed single instance via `readlink node_modules/react`). - Bumping Next 14.2.0 → 14.2.35 via pnpm `overrides`. - Deleting `apps/*/.next` before every rebuild. - Disabling the `next-intl` plugin entirely. - Replacing all providers in the root layout with a bare `
{children}
`. - Replacing the homepage with `export default () =>

x

`. ### Partial workaround (not a fix) Adding `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` to the root layout pushes past the `useContext` crash, then fails differently with: ``` PageNotFoundError: Cannot find module for page: /_document ``` This suggests the RSC dispatcher is only missing on the SSG code path, not on the dynamic SSR path. ### Hypothesis pnpm's symlinked workspace `node_modules` layout is interacting badly with Next 14's internal `AsyncLocalStorage`-based React dispatcher registration during SSG worker processes. The production runtime calls `useContext` before the dispatcher is populated. Reproducer reliably fails across 4 apps in the same workspace, on 2 Next versions, with pinned single-copy React. If someone on the Next team can confirm, it would be helpful to know whether pnpm `shamefully-hoist=true` or `node-linker=hoisted` resolves it — we have not yet tested those because they would change our install semantics project-wide.

title: Bug: Runtime 500 - clientReferenceManifest undefined for server-only pages in Next.js 15.5.18
body:
## Bug: Runtime 500 - `clientReferenceManifest` undefined for server-only pages in Next.js 15.5.18 ### Link to the code that reproduces this issue See reproduction steps below (minimal example included) ### To Reproduce **Minimal reproduction:** 1. Create Next.js 15.5.18 app with App Router: ```bash npx create-next-app@15.5.18 --typescript --app --no-src-dir my-app cd my-app ``` 2. Create a server-only page without client components: ```typescript // app/(marketing)/page.tsx import type { Metadata } from "next"; export const metadata: Metadata = { title: "Home Page", }; export default function HomePage() { return (

Hello World

This is a server-only page with no client components.

); } ``` 3. Build and start production server: ```bash npm run build npm start ``` 4. Navigate to `http://localhost:3000` → **500 Internal Server Error** 5. Check server logs: ``` Error [InvariantError]: Invariant: Expected clientReferenceManifest to be defined. This is a bug in Next.js. at k (.next/server/app/(marketing)/page.js:1:4757) at m (.next/server/app/(marketing)/page.js:1:7389) at n (.next/server/app/(marketing)/page.js:2:1780) at responseGenerator (.next/server/app/(marketing)/page.js:2:1918) ``` ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current:** - Build succeeds ✅ - Production runtime crashes with 500 ❌ - Error: `"Expected clientReferenceManifest to be defined. This is a bug in Next.js."` - Affects server-only pages without client components **Expected:** - Server-only pages should work at runtime - `clientReferenceManifest` should not be required for pages without client components ### Provide environment information ``` Operating System: Platform: darwin (macOS) Arch: arm64 Version: Darwin 24.5.0 Binaries: Node: 25.9.0 npm: 10.9.2 Relevant Packages: next: 15.5.18 react: 19.2.3 react-dom: 19.2.3 @sentry/nextjs: 10.53.1 (optional, but may trigger the issue) typescript: 5.8.3 Next.js Config: output: N/A ``` **next.config.js:** ```javascript const { withSentryConfig } = require("@sentry/nextjs"); const nextConfig = { // Standard config }; module.exports = withSentryConfig(nextConfig, { org: "quote-anvil", project: "javascript-nextjs", silent: !process.env.CI, widenClientFileUpload: false, // Disabled due to ENOENT tunnelRoute: "/monitoring", webpack: { automaticVercelMonitors: true, treeshake: { removeDebugLogging: true, }, }, }); ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) - App Router - Runtime (production) - Build output ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) - `next start` (local) - Vercel (Deployed) ### Additional context **Deep dive:** 1. **Build artifacts:** - `.next/server/app/(marketing)/page.js` exists - `.next/server/app/(marketing)/page.js.nft.json` references `page_client-reference-manifest.js` - `.next/server/app/(marketing)/page_client-reference-manifest.js` does NOT exist 2. **Pattern:** - Pages with client components generate proper manifests and work fine - Pages without client components don't generate manifests and crash at runtime - Examples working: `/pricing`, `/features` (have client components) - Examples broken: `/` (root), `/dashboard` (server-only until auth check) 3. **Build vs Runtime:** - Build succeeds (no errors) - Runtime crashes when accessing affected pages - This is a **production-only** issue (or appears in `next start` but not `next dev`) **Attempted workarounds:** 1. ❌ Create empty manifest placeholders → Build succeeds, runtime still crashes 2. ❌ Remove `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` → No effect 3. ❌ Wrap page in `'use client'` boundary → Manifest still empty, runtime crashes **Successful workaround:** - Downgrade to Next.js 15.4.x or 14.2.x (not tested yet due to React 19 peer dependency conflicts) **Related issues:** - #82229 (mixed routers, similar error) - nextjs/saas-starter#174 (build-time, similar error) **Impact:** - Production sites return 500 on affected pages - Critical severity for landing pages - No data loss or security impact **Deployment context:** - Vercel production deployments - Build succeeds, runtime fails - Multiple consecutive deploys affected (9 in our case) --- This appears to be a regression in Next.js 15.5.x where the build process incorrectly assumes all pages need `clientReferenceManifest` files, even server-only pages. The `.nft.json` file references these manifests, but they're not generated, causing runtime crashes when Next.js tries to load them. The error message itself acknowledges this: `"This is a bug in Next.js."` Would appreciate guidance on: 1. Is this a known issue with a fix in progress? 2. Should server-only pages require manifests in Next.js 15.5? 3. Is there a configuration to disable manifest generation for specific pages?

title: stylesheet could not be loaded - page.css error
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/w4ovt/nextjs-css-chunk-bug-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the repo
2. npm install
3. npm run build
4. npm run start
5. Visit http://localhost:3000 and open DevTools
6. Observe the phantom page.css warning in Console/Network

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behavior:
When running the minimal reproduction in production mode, the browser console displays a warning stating that the page.css stylesheet could not be loaded (e.g.,
Style sheet could not be loaded: http://localhost:3000/_next/static/css/app/page.css...).
This occurs even though the file is present, loads with a 200 status, and all page styles are correctly applied. The warning appears in the Console and the Network tab shows the CSS file as successfully loaded. No manual <link> tags or nonstandard stylesheet imports are used—only standard Next.js CSS modules.

Expected behavior:
There should be no browser warning when the CSS chunk is present, loads successfully, and is applied to the page. The browser should not report a failed stylesheet load if the file is served with a 200 status and styles are rendered as expected.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 24.5.0: Tue Apr 22 19:54:25 PDT 2025; root:xnu-11417.121.6~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6020
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 12
Binaries:
  Node: 22.15.0
  npm: 10.9.2
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 15.3.3 // Latest available version is detected (15.3.3).
  eslint-config-next: 13.5.11
  react: 18.3.1
  react-dom: 18.3.1
  typescript: 5.8.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

CSS, Runtime, Output

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

    This bug occurs in a minimal reproduction using Next.js 15.3.3, the App Router, and a CSS module imported in the root route.

    The phantom page.css warning was the original reason for upgrading from Next.js 14.2 to the latest version. The issue persists after the upgrade.

    The reproduction includes only essential files: layout.tsx, page.tsx, ActivationTable.tsx, ActivationTable.module.css, and a minimal NavBar component.

    No manual <link> tags or non-standard CSS imports are used—only standard Next.js CSS module imports.

    The warning appears in the browser console even though the file is present, loads with a 200 status, and all styles are applied as expected.

    The issue is reproducible on both Apple Silicon macOS (Sonoma) and Intel macOS, in Chrome and Firefox.

    The bug persists after clearing .next and node_modules, and after restoring all relevant project files from the main production codebase.

    No custom webpack or Next.js config is used beyond the default generated by create-next-app.

    My workflow emphasizes accessibility, code audits, and minimal, professional reproductions for bug reporting.

    I am happy to test with canary releases or provide further details if needed.

@w4ovt the repository you shared is private.

What is the content type in the response headers of the failed resource?

The `Content-Type` in the response headers for `/page.css` is:

The file returns a 200 OK status and is served with the correct `text/css` content type, but the browser still displays the “stylesheet could not be loaded” warning.

title: [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: require() of ES Module `shiki` when using `14.2.x`

https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat/tree/arvinxx-patch-1

#### Clone  Repo

```
git clone https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-chat
```

#### Checkout branch

```
git checkout arvinxx-patch-1
```

#### install deps

```
pnpm install / bun install
```

#### run build

```
npm run build
```

    at 13076 (/Users/arvinxx/CodeProjects/LobeHub/lobe-chat/.next/server/app/chat/(mobile)/mobile/page.js:1:835)

title: Slow Page Transitions and Infinite Loading with Internal Navigation Using Link Component in Next.js 14.2

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/

### To Reproduce

1. Start the application in development mode (next dev).
2. Navigate between pages using the Link component from 'next/link'.
3. Expected: Immediate transition with loading indicators appearing without delay.
4. Actual: There is a 2-3 second delay before any loading indicators appear.

6. Click on a link that directs to the current page you are on.
7. Expected: The page should either do nothing or refresh quickly without issues.
8. Actual: The application enters an infinite loading state where the page tries to reload but never completes.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current Behavior:

1. Navigating to a different page shows a delay of approximately 2-3 seconds before loading indicators appear.
2. Clicking on a link to the current page results in infinite loading.

Expected Behavior:

1. Page transitions should be near-instantaneous with loading indicators appearing immediately.
2. Clicking a link to the current page should not cause infinite loading; instead, it should refresh the page quickly or do nothing.

top_comments:
Hi @NavOrange! Thank you for the report.

I took a look at the provided reproduction, and I believe the behavior you're seeing is because your `@form` slot doesn't have a root level Page component (ie `@form/page.tsx`). 

When you first load the `/` page, since there's no `@form/page.tsx` file, it uses `@form/default.tsx` instead. However, on a soft-navigation (such as when using `redirect(...)` or clicking a `<Link />`), the router's behavior is to try and match a Page component on the requested URL. If it can't find one, it will keep around whatever was previously rendered. We fixed a fair number of parallel routes bugs in 14.2, so it's quite possible the behavior was incorrectly working previously.

Here's a video where I took your reproduction and added a `@form/page.tsx` component that just renders `null`:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/assets/1939140/ecc223bd-8653-4706-b98c-53214175f184

More about this behavior can be found [here](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/parallel-routes#active-state-and-navigation).

Please let me know if you're not able to get this to work and I can re-open this issue. Thank you!

title: optimizePackageImports' caches index.ts files (dev and build) when they resolve to source files outside node_modules.
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/threehams/next-optimize-caching

### To Reproduce

Dev caching:
1. Run `npm run dev`
2. Add a syntax error to `ui/index.ts`

Build caching:
1. Run `npm run build`
2. Rename `ui/Button.tsx` to `ui/CounterButton.tsx`, and update imports in `ui/index.ts`
3. Run `npm run build` again

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current:
Dev caching: The syntax error is not reported. The dev server caches the contents of `index.ts` file until server restart.

Build caching:
```
./ui/index.ts
Module not found: Can't resolve './Button'
```
The build caches the `index.ts` file permanently, and will fail until the `.next` directory is deleted.

Expected:
The [Next.js 14.2 release notes](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-14-2#tree-shaking) encourage using `optimizePackageImports: ['package-name']` to optimize barrel files. When these files are outside `node_modules`, the imports should be re-evaluated when those `index.ts` files have changed on disk, in both dev and production builds.

title: `next build --webpack` (v16): `/_not-found` executed at build time + Google Font `Retrying 1/3...` visible — both absent in `next build` (Turbopack) — not seen in v14.2 webpack
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue https://github.com/chandra2607/nextjs-webpack-turbopack-issue.git ### To Reproduce ```bash git clone https://github.com/chandra2607/nextjs-webpack-turbopack-issue.git cd nextjs-webpack-turbopack-issue # Turbopack (next build) docker build --build-arg BUILD_CMD=build -t repro-turbo . 2>&1 | tee out-turbo.txt # Webpack (next build --webpack) docker build --build-arg BUILD_CMD=build:webpack -t repro-webpack . 2>&1 | tee out-webpack.txt # Compare grep "not-found\|Retrying\|Generating static\|ƒ" out-webpack.txt grep "not-found\|Retrying\|Generating static\|ƒ" out-turbo.txt ``` ### Current vs. Expected behavior **Current behavior:** - `next build --webpack`: webpack's static generation worker **executes not-found.tsx** at build time (side effects fire, fetches run) and logs `Retrying 1/3...` for transient Google Font download failures - `next build` (Turbopack): static generation worker **never enters not-found.tsx** and emits no retry logs — the component is silently skipped - Both produce the same final output: `ƒ /_not-found (Dynamic)` **Expected behavior:** Both bundlers should behave identically for `/_not-found` during the build. If the route is dynamic, neither should probe-render it. If one does, both should — so build-time side effects are predictable regardless of which bundler is used. ### Provide environment information ```bash Next.js: 16.2.1 Node: 22-alpine3.20 (Docker) React: 19.0.0 OS: Linux x86_64 ``` ### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) Webpack, Turbopack, Font (next/font) ### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply) next build (local) ### Additional context Hi everyone — I've been digging into some weird build log differences between `next build --webpack` and `next build` (Turbopack) and wanted to write up what I found in case others have run into the same thing or can add context. There are two separate observations below. I'm not 100% sure whether either of these is a bug, a regression, or intentional — just sharing the data. --- ## Observation 1 — `not-found.tsx` component body appears to run at build time with webpack, but not with Turbopack ### What I noticed When I run `next build --webpack`, I can see the body of my `not-found.tsx` getting executed during "Generating static pages" — even though `/_not-found` ends up classified as `ƒ (Dynamic)` in the build output. When I switch to `next build` (Turbopack), nothing in `not-found.tsx` runs at build time at all. Both builds show the same final route table. Both produce: ``` Route (app) ┌ ƒ / └ ƒ /_not-found ƒ (Dynamic) server-rendered on demand ``` ### Repro component (`not-found.tsx`) To keep things simple I stripped it down to a fully synchronous, no-async, no-fetch component: ```tsx export default function NotFound() { console.log("[not-found] component evaluated"); console.log("[not-found] rendering"); return (

404 - Page Not Found

); } ``` ### Webpack build output ``` Generating static pages using 1 worker (0/1) ... [not-found] component evaluated [not-found] rendering ✓ Generating static pages using 1 worker (1/1) in 320ms ``` The component body runs during build. ### Turbopack build output ``` Generating static pages using 1 worker (0/1) ... ✓ Generating static pages using 1 worker (1/1) in 230ms ``` No logs at all — the component wasn't touched. ### What happens when `not-found.tsx` has a network call With a `fetch("http://missing-service:4005/test", { cache: "no-store" })` inside: ``` [not-found] component evaluated [not-found] fetching remote data [fetchRemoteData] about to fetch http://missing-service:4005/test [fetchRemoteData] fetch failed (expected): Dynamic server usage: Route /_global-error ... ``` Turbopack: nothing. No logs, no fetch attempt. ### Why this matters If your `not-found.tsx` (or any component it imports) has side effects — reading env vars during module init, opening a DB connection, making a health-check request — those things appear to silently fire at build time under webpack but not under Turbopack. Code that's only been tested with `next build` could behave differently in environments that use `next build --webpack`. I also tried `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` — it didn't change the behavior for either bundler. **Has anyone else seen this, or can confirm whether this is expected behavior?** --- ## Observation 2 — `Retrying 1/3...` shows up in webpack builds but not Turbopack when using `next/font/google` ### What I noticed When `next/font/google` is in `layout.tsx`, I mostly see this during the webpack compilation phase: ``` Creating an optimized production build ... Retrying 1/3... ✓ Compiled successfully in 10.9s ``` This log never shows up in Turbopack builds. ### Full example from a Docker build (`node:22-alpine3.20`) **Webpack:** ``` ▲ Next.js 16.2.1 (webpack) Creating an optimized production build ... Retrying 1/3... ✓ Compiled successfully in 10.9s ``` **Turbopack:** ``` ▲ Next.js 16.2.1 (Turbopack) Creating an optimized production build ... ✓ Compiled successfully in 5.7s ``` **due to this issue , the overall build time takes longer to complete.** **Has anyone else seen `Retrying 1/3...` in their webpack builds, especially in Docker or CI environments?** --- ## Comparison with Next.js 14.2 Neither of these behaviors appeared in `next build --webpack` on Next.js 14.2. The `[not-found] component evaluated` logs were absent and `Retrying 1/3...` was not reliably reproducible under the same Docker setup (`node:22-alpine3.20`). Both started showing up after upgrading to 16.x. Not sure if this is a regression or an intentional change in how the static generation worker handles `/_not-found` and how the font fetcher is implemented — mentioning it in case it helps narrow things down. --- ## Environment - Next.js: 16.2.1 - Node: 22 (Alpine 3.20 in Docker, native for local) - React: 19.x - OS: Linux (Docker) / macOS (local) ## Related issues - [#76473](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/76473) — Next.js build in GitHub Actions fails due to failed Google Fonts fetching - [#91653](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/91653) — Turbopack Google Fonts `http2 feature is not enabled` on some platforms (16.2) - [#86390](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/86390) — Turbopack crashes when Route Handler calls `notFound()` - [#62228](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/62228) — `not-found.tsx` SSR differences

title: Cookies, logout/auth issue after 14.2
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

none

### To Reproduce

1. We have an server-side function that makes request to API to de-authenticate/logout an user. 

```
    const response = await fetch(`${API}/api/v1${url}`, {
      headers: {
        ...(cookie && {
          Cookie: `COOKIE_NAME=${cookies().get('COOKIE_NAME')?.value ?? ''};`
        }),
        ...(formdata ? {} : { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }),
      },
      method,
      body: (body instanceof FormData) ? body : JSON.stringify(body),
      next: {
        revalidate,
      },
    });
```
COOKIE_NAME here is the sessionId, that is sent with each request.
Cookie revalidate is set to 0. We use this function to all API related requests. 

Backend is written in PHP.


### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behaviour:
The logout feature works only SOMETIMES. Aprox 4 in 5 requests to de-authenticate session are ignored.
It did work without problems before 14.2. I have tested both version and the requests are same, the cookies are sent correctly.
The server DOES respond same in both versions.
This looks like an API problem, but it is not. After 2 day investigation, we realised our older version is working fine, the POSTMAN is working fine and we found out that migrating to 14.2 is what breaks our logout feature.

We noticed this is an issue in build and also dev.

Expected:
Cookies be working without issues.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Next.js v14.2.3.
Custom server.js
Running with "bun"
Reproduced on multiple machines (OSX/Linux)
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not sure

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local)

### Additional context

_No response_

title: Multiple loading.tsx files causes extra transition when revalidating with server actions on 14.2.x+
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/Xexr/revalidate-bug

### To Reproduce

`npm install` to install all dependencies.
`npm run dev` to start the server.

Open [http://localhost:3000/example](http://localhost:3000/example) with your browser

Click the button and you will see that a loading transition is briefly shown on the first press but not on any subsequent presses. This behaviour didn't previously occur with 14.1.4, the first press (and subsequent presses) would revalidate the data without any loading transitions.

The effect in a bigger application is that when a user first invokes a server action, they get a jarring 'refresh' where previously they didn't.

This now appears to happen where multiple layout.tsx and loading.tsx files are present. Remove one of the loading.tsx files and you will see that behaviour reverts to the expected behaviour. I'm not sure if this is part of the root cause, or just masking it by removing a transition.

You can see a vercel deployed example here:

https://revalidate-bug-nine.vercel.app/example

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current (the problem)**

With Next 14.2.x+, when I click the revalidate button, the loading icon now appears for the first press.

Hard refresh (F5) to see the behaviour again.

**Expected behavior**

Previously, with Next 14.1.4, when I clicked the revalidate button, the data would revalidate 'behind the scenes' and no loading icon would show for the first press or subsequent presses.

### Provide environment information

```bash

  Arch: x64
  Version: #1 SMP Thu Jan 11 04:09:03 UTC 2024

  react-dom: 18.3.1
  typescript: 5.4.5
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```


### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Navigation

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Works as expected on 14.1.4

Bug appears to be introduced from 14.2.x onwards

- The file `.next/server/app/_not-found_client-reference-manifest.js` exists

---

title: Turbopack fails to load valid .mjs module with UTF-8 error
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/utsuboco/r3f-perf/blob/752adc19edbcabc43fc917519c5366718fa0b9d0/src/components/TextsHighHZ.tsx#L10

### To Reproduce

### Description
Turbopack is failing to load a valid .mjs module that exports a base64 string. The module is from [r3f-perf](https://github.com/utsuboco/r3f-perf)  package and contains a valid JavaScript file that exports a base64-encoded font string.

### Error Message

```sh
Module not found: Can't resolve '../roboto.woff.mjs'
8 | import as THREE from "three";
9 | import { useEvent } from "@utsubo/events";
> 10 | import localFont from "../roboto.woff.mjs";
| ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
11 | import { getPerf } from "../store.mjs";
failed to convert rope into string
Caused by:
invalid utf-8 sequence of 1 bytes from index 11
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

### Expected Behavior
The file should load successfully as it's a valid ES module that simply exports a string:

```js
javascript
// Content of roboto.woff.mjs
const localFont = "data:font/woff;base64,..."
export { localFont as default };
```

### Actual Behavior
Turbopack appears to be attempting UTF-8 validation before module parsing, causing it to fail on what should be a valid JavaScript file. The same file loads correctly when using webpack.

Their package is Typescript and builds for CJS and ESM. I tried aliasing and it failed.

title: Incorrect XML Namespace in sitemap.ts for Next.js 14.2
body:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/xoocode/next-sitemap-namespace-example

### To Reproduce

1. Clone this repository.
2. Build the project.
3. Visit `localhost:3000/sitemap.xml` in a Chrome browser.
4. The browser will not render the XML correctly.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current Behavior:
The sitemap.xml file generated by Next.js 14.2 contains incorrect namespace declarations. Specifically, the namespace for xhtml:link is defined as `xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"`, causing the XML to render incorrectly in Chrome. Apparently [http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml](url) does not include the xhtml:link definition.

Expected Behavior:
The sitemap.xml file should contain the correct namespace declaration for xhtml:link, allowing the XML to render correctly in browsers. The correct namespace should be `xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml11/xhtml11_schema.html"`.

title: PANIC: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value at query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218 (batched concurrent findUnique, client engine 7.8.0)
body:
## Bug description

In production (Next.js 16 App Router on Railway), a burst of concurrent requests to the same page caused **28 `PrismaClientRustPanicError` crashes within a ~42-second window**, all panicking at the same spot in the new query compiler:

```
panicked at query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218:51:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```

Key observations:

- The crashing queries are plain `findUnique` calls with nested relation `select`s (one-to-many + two to-one relations). The same queries succeed 99.9% of the time.
- The panic only occurred during a concurrency burst, and the debug logs show `prisma:client:clientEngine batch query plan cache miss` immediately around the panics — so this looks related to the **automatic batching of concurrent `findUnique` calls** in the client engine. The compiled query in the crash report contains `@parent$...` placeholder params and `"canAssumeStrictEquality": true`, consistent with the batched/dataloader path.
- Different models were affected in the same burst (both `prisma.event.findUnique()` and `prisma.user.findUnique()` invocations panicked), so it is not specific to one model.
- The panic is **transient**: the process was NOT restarted, and the same queries succeeded again seconds later. So despite the "non-recoverable" wording, the engine recovers on its own; only the in-flight requests fail.

## How to reproduce

I could not reproduce it deterministically — it needed a real concurrency burst (likely a crawler hitting the same uncached page in parallel). Shape of the crashing call:

```ts
await prisma.event.findUnique({
  where: { id },
  select: {
    id: true,
    userId: true,
    title: true,
    description: true,
    eventDate: true,
    visibility: true,
    unpublishedByAdminAt: true,
    status: true,
    mood: true,
    locationCity: true,
    weatherEmoji: true,
    weatherDesc: true,
    weatherTemp: true,
    photoUrl: true,
    tags: true,
    updatedAt: true,
    companionNote: true,
    companionGeneratedAt: true,
    photos: { orderBy: { order: "asc" }, select: { id: true, url: true, order: true, caption: true } },
    category: { select: { slug: true, name: true, emoji: true } },
    user: { select: { name: true, username: true, image: true, deletedAt: true, suspendedAt: true } },
  },
})
```

Run many of these concurrently for the same / different ids (so the client batches them) while the batch query plan cache is cold.

## Relevant schema (trimmed)

```prisma
model Event {
  id         String    @id @default(cuid())
  userId     String
  user       User      @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  categoryId String?
  category   Category? @relation(fields: [categoryId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  title       String
  description String?   @db.Text
  eventDate   DateTime
  status      EventStatus     @default(done)
  visibility  EventVisibility @default(private)
  tags        String[] @default([])
  photos      EventPhoto[]
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  // ... more scalar fields and relations omitted
}

model EventPhoto {
  id      String @id @default(cuid())
  eventId String
  event   Event  @relation(fields: [eventId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  url     String
  order   Int
  caption String?
}
```

## Logs (excerpt)

```
prisma:client:clientEngine query plan executed
prisma:client:clientEngine batch query plan cache miss
prisma:client:request_handler {"clientVersion":"7.8.0","name":"PrismaClientRustPanicError"}
prisma:client:request_handler {"clientVersion":"7.8.0","name":"PrismaClientRustPanicError"}
prisma:client:clientEngine failed to disconnect: {}
prisma:client:clientEngine batch query plan cache miss

⨯ Error [PrismaClientRustPanicError]:
Invalid `prisma.user.findUnique()` invocation:

panicked at query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218:51:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```

(The auto-generated crash report with the full compiled query plan is available; happy to attach more of it on request.)

## Environment & setup

- OS: Linux (Railway container)
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Node.js version: v24.10.0
- Driver adapter: `@prisma/adapter-pg` 7.8.0 (with `pg` Pool, max 10)
- Framework: Next.js 16.2.4 (App Router, standalone server)
- `previewFeatures = ["driverAdapters"]`, default `engineType = "client"` (query compiler)

## Prisma Version

```
prisma: 7.8.0
@prisma/client: 7.8.0
```
top_comments:
**Root cause found — minimal reproduction.**

The panic is triggered when **two or more `findUnique` calls whose unique value is `undefined` are issued concurrently** (same tick), so they enter the dataloader batch path. A single such call is correctly rejected by validation (`PrismaClientValidationError`), but the **batched path bypasses that validation** and the query compiler panics at `query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218` (`QuerySingle::new` → `first.get_single_key().unwrap()` on a filter with zero keys after the undefined value is stripped).

```ts
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString }) })

const bad = () => prisma.user.findUnique({
  where: { id: undefined as unknown as string },
  select: { id: true, posts: { select: { id: true } } },
})

// Single call: PrismaClientValidationError (correct)
// Two+ concurrent calls: PrismaClientRustPanicError at selection.rs:218
await Promise.allSettled([bad(), bad(), bad()])
```

Output on 7.8.0 (`@prisma/adapter-pg`, postgres):
```
0 PrismaClientRustPanicError panicked at query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218:51
1 PrismaClientRustPanicError panicked at query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218:51
2 PrismaClientRustPanicError panicked at query-compiler/core/src/query_document/selection.rs:218:51
```

Worse, innocent queries sharing the batch window fail as collateral: `Promise.allSettled([bad(), good(), bad(), good()])` → the `good()` calls reject too. In our production app a single client with a stale auth cookie (`userId === undefined`) calling `auth()` several times per render was enough to 500 every page for that user.

Expected behavior: the batched path should reject `undefined` unique values with the same `PrismaClientValidationError` as the single-query path.
Wasn't Prisma rewritten in Rust?

Do you want to overwrite the schema to the file? ... yes 🚀 Schema was overwritten successfully! ``` should: detect existing ./prisma/schema.prisma safely parse the auth configuration generate or update schema if needed complete successfully without any Prisma runtime errors such as: ``` PrismaClientConstructorValidationError .prisma/client/default module resolution errors ``` # Actual Behivour ### Frequency Intermittent / Random ### Does this occur in development or production? The issue started appearing after moving to: - Prisma v7 - Next.js 15 - Better Auth latest CLI ### Workaround --- ### Where does this issue happen? ```md id="zrqcc3" The issue occurs in a Next.js 15 project using: - Prisma v7 - Better Auth - PostgreSQL - App Router Specifically during Better Auth CLI schema generation. ``` The only workaround I found was avoiding PrismaClient initialization during module import time. Instead of initializing Prisma directly: ```ts const prisma = new PrismaClient() // when Trying to create or use New PrismaClient got ERR or globalThis.prisma ?? new PrismaClient() I had to avoid initialization entirely in the shared module used by Better Auth CLI. Example workaround: export function getDb() { return globalThis.prisma; } ``` ### Prisma Schema & Queries ````md id="x0d5g6" generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" output = "../src/generated/prisma" } datasource db { provider = "postgresql" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } ### And Db.ts import { PrismaClient } from "@/generated/prisma/client"; declare global { var prisma: PrismaClient | undefined; } export function getDb() { return globalThis.prisma; // Here Where Issue Only Resolve Just by using Global } ### Prisma Config ```ts // Add your `prisma.config.ts` ``` ### Logs & Debug Info ``` // Debug logs here ``` ```bash npx @better-auth/cli generate ``` Error 1: ```text PrismaClientConstructorValidationError: Using engine type "client" requires either "adapter" or "accelerateUrl" ``` Error 2: ```text Error: Cannot find module '.prisma/client/default' ``` ### Environment & Setup - **OS:** - **Database:** - **Node.js version:** ### Prisma Version ``` // Prisma version output Prisma schema loaded from prisma\schema.prisma. prisma : 7.8.0 @prisma/client : 7.8.0 Operating System : win32 Architecture : x64 Node.js : v22.13.1 TypeScript : 5.9.3 Query Compiler : enabled PSL : @prisma/prisma-schema-wasm 7.8.0-6.3c6e192761c0362d496ed980de936e2f3cebcd3a Schema Engine : schema-engine-cli 3c6e192761c0362d496ed980de936e2f3cebcd3a (at node_modules\@prisma\engines\schema-engine-windows.exe) Default Engines Hash : 3c6e192761c0362d496ed980de936e2f3cebcd3a Studio : 0.27.3 ```
top_comments:
I was able to reproduce this issue on a clean project. I found two distinct error scenarios depending on the schema configuration, plus additional TypeScript errors not mentioned in the original report.

---

**Environment**
- OS: Fedora Linux 43
- Node.js: v24.13.1
- Prisma: 7.8.0
- @prisma/client: 7.8.0
- @better-auth/cli: 1.4.21
- Next.js: 15
- Database: PostgreSQL

---

**Reproduction steps**

1. Create a new Next.js 15 project
2. Install `prisma@7`, `@prisma/client@7`, and `better-auth`
3. Run `npx prisma init`
4. Configure `schema.prisma` with a custom output path:

```prisma
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
  output   = "../src/generated/prisma"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL") // see Scenario A vs B below
}
```

5. Create `src/lib/db.ts`:

```ts
import { PrismaClient } from "@/generated/prisma/client";

declare global {
  var prisma: PrismaClient | undefined;
}

export const prisma = globalThis.prisma ?? new PrismaClient();
```

6. Create `src/lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { prismaAdapter } from "better-auth/adapters/prisma";
import { prisma } from "./db";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: prismaAdapter(prisma, {
    provider: "postgresql",
  }),
});
```

7. Run `npx prisma generate`
8. Run `npx @better-auth/cli generate`

---

**Scenario A — with `url` in `schema.prisma` (reproduces Case 1)**

When `url = env("DATABASE_URL")` is present in `schema.prisma`, the following error occurs:

```
[#better-auth]: Couldn't read your auth config. PrismaClientConstructorValidationError: Using engine type "client" requires either "adapter" or "accelerateUrl" to be provided to PrismaClient constructor.
Read more at https://pris.ly/d/client-constructor
    at new t (.../node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/client.js:70:1808)
    at .../src/lib/db.ts:7:54
    at async import (.../jiti/dist/jiti.cjs:1:187718)
    at async .../src/lib/auth.ts:3:11
```

**Scenario B — without `url` in `schema.prisma`**

When `url` is removed from `schema.prisma` (e.g. when datasource is handled via `prisma.config.ts`), a different error occurs:

```
[#better-auth]: Couldn't read your auth config. PrismaClientInitializationError: `PrismaClient` needs to be constructed with a non-empty, valid `PrismaClientOptions`
    at new t (.../node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/client.js:70:1527)
    at .../src/lib/db.ts:7:54
    at async import (.../jiti/dist/jiti.cjs:1:187718)
    at async .../src/lib/auth.ts:3:11
```

---

**Additional findings — TypeScript errors on `PrismaClient` constructor**

Beyond the CLI errors, Prisma v7 also introduces TypeScript errors when constructing `PrismaClient` directly:

- `new PrismaClient()` → `TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 0`
- `new PrismaClient({})` → `TS2345: Argument of type '{}' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Subset<PrismaClientOptions, PrismaClientOptions>'`

This suggests Prisma v7 changed the `PrismaClient` constructor to require a non-empty `options` argument, which is a breaking change from previous versions.

---

**Root cause analysis**

The stack trace in both scenarios shows `better-auth/cli` uses `jiti` to dynamically import `auth.ts` at CLI runtime, which triggers `db.ts`, which calls `new PrismaClient()` at module load time. In Prisma v7 with engine type `"client"`, this initialization requires either `adapter` or `accelerateUrl` — neither of which is available in a CLI context.

The two error scenarios are independent — removing `url` from `schema.prisma` does not resolve the CLI error. The root cause is the breaking change in the Prisma v7 `PrismaClient` constructor.

---

**Workaround**

The workaround mentioned in the original report works in my setup as well — wrapping `PrismaClient` initialization inside a function instead of initializing at module level:

```ts
export function getDb() {
  return globalThis.prisma;
}
```

However, this is not an intuitive pattern and may not be obvious to users migrating from Prisma v6.

title: Solution for the compatibility issue in the modules query_engine_bg.js and query_engine_bg.wasm when generating with @prisma/client: Failed to load module
body: ### Bug description ## 🗣️ [ Translated ] English US First of all, this issue is about the error that is even addressed in the **unjs/unwasm** issue (["prisma compatibility #21"](https://github.com/unjs/unwasm/issues/21)), where when running the project, regardless of whether it is NodeJS or Bun, the following errors are triggered: **1°. Import error of the file `query_engine_bg.js` in the file `node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js`** ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js:199:27 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.js' 197 | defineDmmfProperty(exports.Prisma, config.runtimeDataModel) 198 | config.engineWasm = { > 199 | getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 200 | getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { 201 | const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default 202 | const engine = (await loader).default ``` **2°. Import error of `query_engine_bg.wasm` in the file `node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light.loader.mjs`** ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs:4:16 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.wasm' 2 | /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! 3 | /* eslint-disable */ > 4 | export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') ``` From what I discovered by analyzing several issues and forum discussions, being the first one to notice this, the bug ironically occurs because the **@prisma/client** feature is cross-platform, where when executing the `prisma generate` command, the files are generated as expected in the `node_modules/.prisma/client` folder but, I am not exactly sure why (I haven’t analyzed prisma’s code yet), the compiler instead of generating a WASM that is cross-platform compatible, ends up generating the native binary of the operating system (which in my case of Windows x64, instead of generating the `query_engine_bg.wasm` file, it generated the file `query_engine-windows.dll.node`). Up to this point it’s not really a problem because, like in this case where it didn’t necessarily become an `.exe` binary, when replacing both `query_engine_bg.js` and `query_engine_bg.wasm` with `query_engine-windows.dll.node`, running the project works correctly; that is, at some level the binary is generated "correctly" (apart from the fact that the name is not standardized, nor does it have the `.wasm` extension), it would simply be enough to fix the import path of both files, or simply generate the files with standardized names and extensions. I know that **prisma** wants to be part of the **edge runtime** and that’s fine, I use this in NextJS projects, the point is only this, the standardization even if cross-platform, regardless of whether it’s WASM or a native binary, as long as it’s correctly referenced by the client generator. And the error becomes even stranger when we define `engineType = "binary"` because, as on my Windows x64 computer, when I executed `prisma generate`, now instead of `query_engine.windows.dll.node` it ended up generating the file `query-engine-windows.exe`, which diverges even more from the WASM purpose. In summary, the bug occurs because **@prisma/client** when the `prisma generate` command is executed, instead of compiling the "Query Engine" into the `query_engine_bg.wasm` file (and its "mapper", the `query_engine_bg.js`) it ends up generating a non-standardized binary, both in terms of naming and extension; and because of this, the JS runtime cannot find the "Query Engine" binary. **Images of my VS Code console** ------ ## 🗣️ [ Original ] Português BR Primeiramente, esse issue trata-se do erro que é até abordado no issue do **unjs/unwasm** (["prisma compatibility #21"](https://github.com/unjs/unwasm/issues/21)), onde ao executar o projeto, independente se este seja NodeJS ou Bun, os seguintes erros são disparados: **1°. Error de importação do arquivo 'query_engine_bg.js' no arquivo 'node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js'** ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js:199:27 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.js' 197 | defineDmmfProperty(exports.Prisma, config.runtimeDataModel) 198 | config.engineWasm = { > 199 | getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 200 | getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { 201 | const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default 202 | const engine = (await loader).default ``` **2°. Erro de importação do 'query_engine_bg.wasm' no arquivo 'node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light.loader.mjs'** ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs:4:16 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.wasm' 2 | /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! 3 | /* eslint-disable */ > 4 | export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') ``` Pelo que descobri analisando diversos issues e conversas em forums, sendo o primeiro a perceber isso, o bug ocorre, ironicamente, pela feature do **@prisma/client** ser multiplataforma, onde ao executar o comando `prisma generate`, os arquivos são gerados como esperado na pasta `node_modules/.prisma/client` mas, não sei ao certo o por que (não analisei o código do prisma ainda), o compilador ao invés de gerar um WASM que é compatível multiplataforma, acaba gerando o binário nativo do sistema operacional (que nem no meu caso de Windows x64, ao invés de gerar o arquivo `query_engine_bg.wasm`, ele acabou gerando o arquivo `query_engine-windows.dll.node`). Até ai não é um problema pois, que nem nesse caso que não se tornou necessariamente um binário `.exe`, ao substituir tanto o `query_engine_bg.js` e `query_engine_bg.wasm` por `query_engine-windows.dll.node`, ao executar o projeto ele funciona corretamente; ou seja, em certo nível o binário e gerado "corretamente" (tirando o fato do nome não ser padronizado, muito menos possuindo a extensão `.wasm`), bastaria corrigir o caminho da importação de ambos os arquivos, ou simplesmente, gerar os arquivos com nome e extensão padronizados. Eu sei que o **prisma** quer fazer parte do **edge runtime** e tudo bem, eu uso isso em projetos NextJS, a questão é somente isso, a padronização mesmo que multiplataforma, independente se seja WASM ou binário nativo, desde que referenciado corretamente pelo gerador do cliente. E o erro se torna mais esquisito quando definimos `engineType = "binary"` pois, que nem no meu computador Windows x64, quando executei o `prisma generate`, agora ao invés de `query_engine.windows.dll.node` ele acabou gerando o arquivo `query-engine-windows.exe`, o que desvia ainda mais do propósito WASM. Resumindo, o bug ocorre pois o **@prisma/client** quando o comando `prisma generate` é executado, ao invés de compilar o "Query Engine" para o arquivo `query_engine_bg.wasm` (e seu "mapeador", o `query_engine_bg.js`) ele acaba gerando um binário despadronizado, tanto no quesito nomenclatura, quanto no quesito extensão; e por causa disso, o runtime JS não consegue encontrar o binário do "Query Engine". **Imagens do meu console do VS Code** ### Severity ⚠️ Major: Breaks core functionality (e.g., migrations fail) ### Reproduction ## 🗣️ [ Translated ] English US To reproduce the bug it is basically necessary to install and minimally use **prisma**. In the case of my development environment (NOTE: I am using Windows 11 x64, 8GB RAM, Intel Core I5), I used **MongoDB Community** locally as a database running in cluster mode. Here I will address the reproduction more directly, both the standard and the anomalous. ### 🪲 Bug of incorrect compilation of the files `query_engine_bg.js` and `query_engine_bg.wasm` 1. Create a **NextJS** project using Bun through the command: `bun create next-app` 2. Follow the configuration steps of **NextJS**: ```pwsh What is your project named? » any Would you like to use TypeScript? » Yes Which linter would you like to use? » ESLint Would you like to use Tailwind CSS? ... No Would you like your code inside a `src/` directory? ... No Would you like to use App Router? (recommended) ... Yes Would you like to use Turbopack? (recommended) » Yes Would you like to customize the import alias (`@/*` by default)? » No ``` 3. After creation and **Bun** finishes managing the **NextJS** packages, add the following dependencies: ```pwsh bun add @prisma/client bun add prisma --save-dev ``` 4. Run the initial **prisma** setup specifying **mongodb** as the provider: ```pwsh bun prisma init --datasource-provider mongodb ``` 5. Configure the connection string with **MongoDB** in the `.env` environment file: ```env DATABASE_URL="mongodb://localhost:27017/mydatabase?retryWrites=true&w=majority" ``` 6. Create a simple schema in `prisma/schema.prisma`, here is a basic example: ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" } datasource db { provider = "mongodb" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } model User { id String @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId uniqueId String @default(uuid()) email String @unique name String? @@map("users") } ``` 7. Ask **prisma** to generate the files by running: `bun prisma generate` 8. In any `page.tsx` of the **NextJS** project, on the **server-side**, program any query with **prisma**. 9. Ask **Bun** to run **NextJS** in development mode using: `bun dev` 10. When accessing the site `http://localhost:3000` (considering that you used the default `page.tsx` from the `app`), the **NextJS** Debug in the browser and in the console will display the error logs: ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js:199:27 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.js' 197 | defineDmmfProperty(exports.Prisma, config.runtimeDataModel) 198 | config.engineWasm = { > 199 | getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 200 | getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { 201 | const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default 202 | const engine = (await loader).default ``` ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs:4:16 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.wasm' 2 | /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! 3 | /* eslint-disable */ > 4 | export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') ``` 11. When accessing the folder `node_modules/.prisma/client`, instead of the expected WASM file (`query_engine_bg.wasm`), the file `query_engine.windows.dll.node` will be present and, also, you will notice the absence of the auxiliary file `query_engine_bg.js`. ### 🐜 "Bug" of platform-specific compilation To reproduce the platform-specific erroneous compilation, just follow the previous steps plus the following: 1. In the `prisma/schema.prisma` file, change the `datasource client` code snippet to: ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" engineType = "binary" } ``` 2. Run the **prisma** generation by executing the command: `bun prisma generate` 3. Access the `node_modules/.prisma/client` folder and the file `query-engine-windows.exe` will be present instead of the previously generated `query_engine.windows.dll.node`. ------- ## 🗣️ [ Original ] Português BR Para reproduzir o bug e necessário basicamente a instalação e uso mínimo do **prisma**. No caso do meu ambiente de desenvolvimento (OBS: estou utilizando Windows 11 x64, 8GB RAM, Intel Core I5), eu utilizei o **MongoDB Community** localmente como banco de dados rodando do modo cluster, aqui vou abordar de forma mais direta a reprodução, tanto a padrão quanto a anômala. ### 🪲 Bug da compilação errônea dos arquivos `query_engine_bg.js` e `query_engine_bg.wasm` 1. Crie um esquema simples no `prisma/schema.prisma`, aqui vou dar um exemplo básico: ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" } datasource db { provider = "mongodb" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } model User { id String @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId uniqueId String @default(uuid()) email String @unique name String? @@map("users") } ``` 7. Mande o **prisma** gerar os arquivos executando: `bun prisma generate` 8. Em qualquer `page.tsx` do projeto **NextJS**, no **server-side**, programe qualquer consulta com o **prisma**. 9. Mande o **Bun** executar o **NextJS** no modo de desenvolvimento usando: `bun dev`. 10. Ao acessar o site `http://localhost:3000` (considerando que utilizou o `page.tsx` padrão do `app`), o Debug do **NextJS** no navegador e no console irão exibir os logs de erro: ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js:199:27 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.js' 197 | defineDmmfProperty(exports.Prisma, config.runtimeDataModel) 198 | config.engineWasm = { > 199 | getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 200 | getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { 201 | const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default 202 | const engine = (await loader).default ``` ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs:4:16 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.wasm' 2 | /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! 3 | /* eslint-disable */ > 4 | export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') ``` 11. Ao acessar a pasta `node_modules/.prisma/client`, ao invés do arquivo WASM esperado (`query_engine_bg.wasm`) estará presente o arquivo `query_engine.windows.dll.node` e, também, se notará a ausência do arquivo auxiliar `query_engine_bg.js`. ### 🐜 "Bug" da compilação específica de plataforma Para reproduzir a compilação errônea específica de plataforma, basta seguir os passos anterior mais os seguintes: 1. No arquivo `prisma/schema.prisma`, altere o trecho de código do `datasource client` para: ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" engineType = "binary" } ``` 2. Execute a geração do **prisma** executando o comando: `bun prisma generate`. 3. Acesse a pasta `node_modules/.prisma/cliente` e o arquivo `query-engine-windows.exe` estará presente ao invés do anteriormente gerado `query_engine.windows.dll.node`. ### Expected vs. Actual Behavior My expectation was that the client would work correctly, executing queries on the **MongoDB** database. However, due to the **@prisma/client** generation error, the outcome was limited to console log outputs: ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm.js:199:27 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.js' 197 | defineDmmfProperty(exports.Prisma, config.runtimeDataModel) 198 | config.engineWasm = { > 199 | getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 200 | getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { 201 | const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default 202 | const engine = (await loader).default ``` ``` ⨯ ./node_modules/.prisma/client/wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs:4:16 Module not found: Can't resolve './query_engine_bg.wasm' 2 | /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! 3 | /* eslint-disable */ > 4 | export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') ``` ### Frequency Consistently reproducible ### Does this occur in development or production? Both development and production ### Is this a regression? Frankly, I cannot recall the exact version of **Prisma** I was using, but until a few months ago, approximately four to six months, **Prisma** was functioning correctly, as expected. However, in the current **version 6.16.1**, this is no longer the case. ### Workaround ## 🗣️ [ Translated ] English US To fix this bug, a few simple steps should be followed after setting up the development environment (still assuming I am using Windows 11 x64). Different operating systems may generate a different name for the WASM file: 1. Run Bun to generate generator with the command: `bun prisma generate` using the default `generator` and `datasource` configuration for **MongoDB**: ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" } datasource db { provider = "mongodb" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } ``` 2. Inside the folder node_modules/.prisma/client, open and modify the file wasm.js by changing the config.engineWasm code to: ```js config.engineWasm = { // * old code: getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine-windows.dll.node'), getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default const engine = (await loader).default return engine } } ``` 3. Then, open and modify the file wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs, changing the default import code to the new one: ```js /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! /* eslint-disable */ // * old code: export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') export default import('./query_engine-windows.dll.node?module') ``` Now, when running the **NextJS** project with the command `bun dev`, it will execute normally. ------- ## 🗣️ [ Original ] Português BR Para corrigir esse bug, deve ser seguidos alguns passos simples após a configuração do ambiente de desenvolvimento (ainda considerando que estou utilizando o Windows 11 x64), pode ser que cada sistema operacional gere um nome diferente para o arquivo WASM: 1. Basta mandar o **Bun** executar a geração do **prisma** com o comando: `bun prisma generate` usando a configuração de `generator` e `datasource` padrão para o **mongodb**: ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" } datasource db { provider = "mongodb" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } ``` 2. Dentro da pasta `node_module/.prisma/client` abra e altere o arquivo `wasm.js` mudando o código `config.engineWasm` para: ```js config.engineWasm = { // * old code: getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine_bg.js'), getRuntime: async () => require('./query_engine-windows.dll.node'), getQueryEngineWasmModule: async () => { const loader = (await import('#wasm-engine-loader')).default const engine = (await loader).default return engine } } ``` 3. Agora, abra e altere o arquivo `wasm-edge-light-loader.mjs` mudando o código `import` padrão para o novo: ```js /* !!! This is code generated by Prisma. Do not edit directly. !!! /* eslint-disable */ // * old code: export default import('./query_engine_bg.wasm?module') export default import('./query_engine-windows.dll.node?module') ``` Pronto, agora ao executar o projeto **NextJS** executando o comando `bun dev`, será executado normalmente. ### Prisma Schema & Queries ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" } datasource db { provider = "mongodb" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } model UserAddress { id String @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId userId String @db.ObjectId userInfo UserInfo @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade) street String number Int complement String? title: Prisma + Next.js (App Router) on Vercel with Prisma Postgres: "Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL" despite env set
body: ### Bug description Even after following [the official guide](https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/nextjs) for Next.js + Prisma and setting DATABASE_URL in Vercel, runtime fails with: ``` Error [PrismaClientInitializationError]: error: Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL. at Object.gu [as resolveDatasourceUrl] (.next/server/app/page.js:97:987) at (.next/server/app/page.js:29:5285) at Proxy.f0 (.next/server/app/page.js:66:5130) at 46277 (.next/server/app/page.js:29:4594) at Object.c [as require] (.next/server/webpack-runtime.js:1:205) at async f (.next/server/app/page.js:170:34734) { clientVersion: '6.13.0', errorCode: undefined, digest: '1000217116' } ``` The app is deployed to Vercel. DATABASE_URL is set to a Prisma Postgres URL like: prisma+postgres://accelerate.prisma-data... (works locally). Link to the doc I followed • https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/nextjs ### What I tried 1. Verified DATABASE_URL exists for both Preview and Production on Vercel. 3. Redeployed after setting envs. 4. Created Turborepo config as above. 7. Locally, everything works (.env with the same prisma+postgres://... URL). ### Questions - Is there a known issue where resolveDatasourceUrl fails to read env("DATABASE_URL") in Vercel builds with Turborepo, even when runtime process.env.DATABASE_URL is set? ### Severity 🔹 Minor: Unexpected behavior, but does not block development ### Reproduction 1. Create Next.js (App Router) + Prisma project. 2. Use Prisma Postgres (Accelerate) connection string for DATABASE_URL (prisma+postgres://...). 3. Deploy to Vercel. 4. Set DATABASE_URL in Vercel (Preview/Production), redeploy. 5. Hit a route that touches Prisma → runtime error: Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL. ### Expected vs. Actual Behavior - Expected behavior: Prisma Client should pick up DATABASE_URL from Vercel runtime env and connect via Accelerate without error. - Actual behavior; Runtime throws Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL, even though vercel env is set and visible to other code (process.env.DATABASE_URL is truthy when checked in a simple route). ### Frequency Consistently reproducible ### Does this occur in development or production? Both development and production ### Is this a regression? I am sorry, I don't know, because I have started my project recently. ### Workaround No workaround found ### Prisma Schema & Queries prisma/schema.prisma ```prisma generator client { provider = "prisma-client-js" output = "../app/generated/prisma" } datasource db { provider = "postgresql" url = env("DATABASE_URL") } ``` lib/prisma.ts ```ts import { PrismaClient } from '../app/generated/prisma' import { withAccelerate } from '@prisma/extension-accelerate' import { withOptimize } from "@prisma/extension-optimize"; const globalForPrisma = global as unknown as { prisma: PrismaClient } const prisma = globalForPrisma.prisma || new PrismaClient().$extends(withAccelerate()).$extends(withOptimize({apiKey: process.env.PRISMA_OPTIMIZE_API_KEY!})) if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') globalForPrisma.prisma = prisma export default prisma ``` package.json ```json "scripts": { "dev": "next dev --turbopack", "build": "next build", "postinstall": "prisma generate --no-engine", "start": "next start", "lint": "next lint" }, ``` turbo.json ```json { "globalEnv": ["DATABASE_URL"] } ``` ### Prisma Config none ### Logs & Debug Info ``` Error [PrismaClientInitializationError]: error: Environment variable not found: DATABASE_URL. at Object.gu [as resolveDatasourceUrl] (.next/server/app/page.js:97:987) at (.next/server/app/page.js:29:5285) at Proxy.f0 (.next/server/app/page.js:66:5130) at 46277 (.next/server/app/page.js:29:4594) at Object.c [as require] (.next/server/webpack-runtime.js:1:205) at async f (.next/server/app/page.js:170:34734) { clientVersion: '6.13.0', errorCode: undefined, digest: '1000217116' } ``` ### Environment & Setup - Prisma Client: 6.13.0 - Next.js (App Router): 15.4.5 - Deployment: Vercel - DB: Prisma Postgres, DATABASE_URL is the prisma+postgres://... form - Vercel Envs: DATABASE_URL configured in Preview and Production; redeployed after changes ### Prisma Version ``` 10.14.0 ```

title: Bug: Prisma Query Engine not bundled in Vercel Serverless (Expo Router, non-Next.js)
body:
### Bug description

Hey all — just confirming that this issue still happens in non-Next.js setups too.
I’m using Expo Router with API routes deployed on Vercel via @expo/server/adapter/vercel, and the Prisma query engine is still not found at runtime — even with binaryTargets = ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"] set.

I had to manually copy libquery_engine-rhel-openssl-3.0.x.so.node from .prisma/client/ into a known path and reference it via binaryPath in new PrismaClient(...).

### Severity

🚨 Critical:  app/website does not work only in production/preview

[
](https://pray-tracker.vercel.app/api/pro)

### Expected vs. Actual Behavior

### 🧪 Notes

- I’m **not using Next.js**, so this is **not related to `optimizePackageImports`**
- Using Prisma version: `6.5.0`
- Vercel server runtime: `rhel-openssl-3.0.x`
- Expo Router + `app/api/xyz+api.ts` API routes

---

### 🙏 Request

Would love better out-of-the-box support for Prisma in **serverless setups without Next.js**, especially Expo Router and other frameworks using custom middleware or handlers (like `createRequestHandler()` from `@expo/server`).

### Frequency

Consistently reproducible

### Does this occur in development or production?

Only in production (e.g., query engine, generated client)

### Is this a regression?

### Prisma Schema & Queries

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = ["driverAdapters","reactNative"]
  binaryTargets = ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"]
}

datasource db {
  provider  = "postgresql"
  url       = env("EXPO_SECRET_DATABASE_URL")
  directUrl = env("EXPO_SECRET_DIRECT_URL")
}

### Logs & Debug Info
```
prisma:error 
Invalid `prisma.pro.findFirst()` invocation:

Prisma Client could not locate the Query Engine for runtime "rhel-openssl-3.0.x".

This is likely caused by a bundler that has not copied "libquery_engine-rhel-openssl-3.0.x.so.node" next to the resulting bundle.
Ensure that "libquery_engine-rhel-openssl-3.0.x.so.node" has been copied next to the bundle or in "node_modules/.prisma/client".

We would appreciate if you could take the time to share some information with us.
Please help us by answering a few questions: https://pris.ly/engine-not-found-bundler-investigation

The following locations have been searched:
  /var/task/node_modules/.prisma/client
  /var/task/dist/server/_expo/functions
  /Users/salah/Documents/projects/pray-tracker/node_modules/@prisma/client
  /var/task/dist/server/.prisma/client
  /tmp/prisma-engines

@SevInf First, I apologize for my delayed response. You were absolutely right about the driver adapters, and I should have followed up sooner.

After investigating further, I actually solved the issue using a different approach that didn't require driver adapters. Here's what worked:

Instead of trying to make Prisma work in Edge Runtime, I implemented a split configuration pattern that separates the Edge and Node.js concerns:

1. Created a lightweight `auth.config.ts` for Edge:
```typescript
export const authConfig = {
  providers: [Google],
  session: { strategy: "database" },
  callbacks: {
    authorized: // Basic routing logic
  }
}
```

2. Simplified the middleware:
```typescript
export default auth

export const config = {
  matcher: ["/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.well-known).*)"]
}
```

3. Kept PrismaAdapter in the main `auth.ts` configuration.

This solution avoids the need for driver adapters entirely by not using Prisma in Edge Runtime at all. The authentication flow now works perfectly with zero errors.

Thank you for your help and patience. This experience taught me to:
1. Respond more promptly to support requests
2. Better understand Edge Runtime limitations
3. Consider simpler solutions before adding complexity

Feel free to close this issue. I hope this resolution helps others who might face similar issues.
