title: Module-level Prisma 8 client hangs on the second request in Cloudflare Workers
body:
### Package and version

@prisma/orm-postgres@8.0.0-rc.9, prisma@8.0.0-rc.13, wrangler 4.131.0

### What happened?

The `src/prisma/db.ts` that `orm init` scaffolds creates one client at module scope:

```ts
export const db = postgres<Contract>({ contractJson, url: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
```

Importing that client from a Cloudflare Worker's `fetch` handler works for exactly one request. The second request hangs and `wrangler dev` reports:

```text
[wrangler:info] GET / 200 OK (1971ms)
✘ [ERROR] Uncaught Error: The Workers runtime canceled this request because it detected that your Worker's code had hung and would never generate a response. Refer to: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/errors/
[wrangler:info] GET / 500 Internal Server Error (90ms)
```

The pattern repeats: request 1 succeeds, request 2 fails, request 3 succeeds, and so on. The cause is the Workers I/O context rule: a socket opened during one request cannot be used by another, and the client's `pg.Pool` keeps the stale socket and hands it to the next request. Nothing in the scaffold, the CLI output, or the client warns about this.

Creating the client inside `fetch` and closing it after the response works, including over TLS to Prisma Postgres:

```ts
const db = postgres<Contract>({ contractJson, url: env.DATABASE_URL });
try {
  // queries
} finally {
  ctx.waitUntil(db.close());
}
```

The `@prisma/orm-postgres/serverless` export (`postgresServerless`) is the per-request client meant for this environment, but it exposes only the SQL builder (`db.sql`) and not `db.orm`, so ORM queries cannot use it.

### What did you expect to happen?

One of:

- The client detects the Workers runtime (or a per-request option) and does not reuse pooled connections across requests.
- `postgresServerless` exposes `db.orm` so Workers users have a supported ORM client.
- At minimum, `orm init` and the Workers docs say that the scaffolded module-level client must not be used from a Worker, and show the per-request pattern.

### Minimal reproduction

1. `npm create cloudflare@latest prisma-cloudflare-worker -- --type=hello-world --lang=ts --git --no-deploy --no-agents`, add `"nodejs_compat"` to `compatibility_flags` in `wrangler.jsonc`.
2. `npx prisma@latest orm init --yes --target postgres --authoring psl`, set `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`, `npx prisma@latest contract emit`, `npx prisma@latest db init`.
3. In `src/index.ts`, `import { db } from "./prisma/db"` and run one `db.orm.public.User.create(...)` per request inside `fetch`.
4. `npx wrangler dev`, then `curl http://localhost:8787/` three times. The second call returns 500 with the "code had hung" error above.
5. Replace the import with a client created inside `fetch` and closed with `ctx.waitUntil(db.close())`. All three calls return 200.

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15
- Node.js: v24.11.1
- wrangler 4.131.0, `compatibility_date` 2026-09-07, `nodejs_compat`
- Database: PostgreSQL 17 local via `localConnectionString`, and Prisma Postgres over TLS (same result)

### Additional context

Found while validating the Prisma 8 Cloudflare Workers guide on 2026-09-10. The guide now creates one client per request and explains why the Worker does not import `src/prisma/db.ts`. A per-request client on Workers also means one connection per request, so a pooling endpoint in front of the database matters more than it does on Node.
top_comments:
hi, i'd like to work on this.

workers cannot reuse a socket across requests, but the module-level postgres() client keeps the pool. therefore request 2 hangs. i'd actually expose db.orm on postgresserverless so workers get a real per-request orm client, and have orm init warn when it scaffolds a module-level client for wrangler.

should postgresserverless grow the full orm surface, or do you want a workers-aware pool that recreates connections per request instead?

title: `prisma-client-js` requests to open cloudflare workers
body:
### Feature Summary

Cloudflare hyperdrive is a database connection pool proxy specifically for workers. It is similar to Vercel's Postgres connection. After testing, I found that the default client allows direct use in Vercel, while in Workers it is required to use a driver adapter.

### Use Cases & Problem Description

The reason for this is simple, Hyperdrive supports proxying Postgres and MySQL. And it doesn't matter how many connections there are;

Driver adapters are very slow at the moment, and workers have node compatibility and wasm support like Vercel Functions. People should be able to use Postgres and MySQL in workers.

### Proposed Solution

https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/deployment/serverless/deploy-to-vercel
Just like in the deploy-to-vercel documentation, do not intercept and output errors when the database is Postgres or MySQL, and start the wasm query engine normally.

### Alternative Solutions

It's faster to complete the adapter drivers for first-class databases, but this takes too long. It completely hinders users from using Prisma normally.

### Potential Considerations

_No response_

### Prisma Version

_No response_

### What part of Prisma does this affect?

None

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Pre-Submission Checklist

- [x] I have **searched existing issues** to make sure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I have **checked the [Prisma roadmap](https://pris.ly/orm-roadmap)** to see if this is already planned

I struggled for a long time before submitting this issue, and did a deployment test in Vercel. I don't understand why Prisma can be used directly in Vercel but not in the worker.

Driver adaptation currently only supports a small number of databases, and there are many bugs and it is not suitable for production environments.

**If there is a MySQL driver, I am willing to use it even if there are bugs** But the reality is that there is no such driver, and when developing for a company, employees do not have the right to choose what database to use. As an employee, you only have the right to use the tool.

----- Not related to the issue, just complaining
Today I spent a lot of time testing and even tried other ORMs. But I still like Prisma, but since last year, Prisma's progress seems to have slowed down. The quarterly roadmap has not been completed.

It used to be pleasant to use Prisma (at that time, many companies did not try serverless, but used traditional hosted deployment, and there would be no problems). Now Prisma is painful, not because it is not easy to use. But more and more technical directions tend to be serverless, and Prisma's tool chain can never keep up.

title: @prisma/adapter-neon ignores schema in the connection string
top_comments: Hi @Raepheles, `schema` query parameter is non-standard Prisma addition that is not understood by `pg` or `neon`. The source code should be https://github.com/prisma/prisma/blob/bb3efede3a584f78522ea4509288eab9dc3c24f8/packages/debug/src/index.ts#L66-L84

@colenh This warning can be safely ignored, it's only a warning from Next.js which detected `process.stderr` in the code but it would not be used once deployed because it would not exist and the conditions would catch that and switch to `console.warn or log`

These warnings appear because Next.js is leveraging Webpack Compiler Hooks to monitor when `process.*` methods are used: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/303d155c08a343ca9c45c80be216417bbe7a0cc2/packages/next/src/build/webpack/plugins/middleware-plugin.ts#L368-L370.

To avoid warnings, we could conditionally import our own Vercel Edge-compatible debug module (without any dependency on `process`), and fall back to using `process.stderr` for other runtimes.
